correctness.rationale: For each prime, exclusion of residues 0 and 1 produces three assignments, yielding the signed CRT identity. At an odd modulus the associated parity sums have odd length and alternating signs; at twice an odd modulus the mod-four character cancels in blocks of four with two remainder terms. The 2-adic branch follows from equal distribution of lifts modulo four. CRT reciprocity gives the two-prime sign and Dirichlet equidistribution gives equal branch densities. A standalone verifier passed exhaustive direct evaluation of n<=2000, 499 odd radical/parity checks and ordered distinct odd prime pairs below 100. All quantifiers and n=1,2 boundary cases are handled.

value.rationale: Renshaw motivates evaluation of T(n) but gives general bounds only; the result replaces them with universal factorization-based finite exact evaluations, isolates two exponents-independent radical corrections, and fully resolves the semiprime sign together with balanced occurrence among primes. These are natural structural answers about the paper's own invariant, not arbitrary numeric cutoffs. No optimal algorithm or downstream cryptography theorem is claimed.
